Code 57/1/3, BIOLOGY (Theory), 3 hours, 70 marks; internal job number 2401-3); idx 1 is the Hindi instructions; every ODD index 3-21 is the Hindi facing page and opens with a Hindi question number (checked on the contact sheet, the text layer, and at full size for idx 11), so no English overflows onto an odd page and the parity never inverts. idx 23 is blank apart from the footer. The paper is born-digital: the text layer was used as a DRAFT only and every row was checked against the full-size page. Instruction (viii) gives no count of internal choices; the roster was built from the marking scheme's bare ORs and confirmed against a printed OR on the page: Q18, Q20, Q21, Q29(a), Q30(a), Q31, Q32, Q33, eight alternatives, none in Section C. Primary marks: A16 + B10 + C21 + D8 + E15 = 70. Section-A key read off the scheme IMAGE (ms idx 2) and independently from the scheme's text layer: BDAABBBCCBBAADCC, 16 of 16 agree. No CBSE void anywhere in the scheme (the only award notes, Q27's medium components and Q31(b)(ii), are conditional). FOLLOWER of 57/1/1: 30 of 45 rows are the opener's questions reshuffled, confirmed on this paper's pages and copied byte for byte (stem, context, options, and the opener's key matches this scheme's on all ten shared MCQs); 15 rows are new to this set (Q1, Q2, Q8, Q9, Q10, Q13, Q17, Q19, Q20a, Q20b, Q21a, Q21b, Q27, Q32a, Q32b). The opener's Q23 figure note says the pedigree has six offspring; both papers draw five, so this paper's Q25 note says five. Every _figure was read on this paper's own page. The paper prints no decimals. Quotes are straight, scientific names plain text (the Biology rules).

NPP = GPP – R

Biodiversity conservation is crucial for maintaining ecological balance and ensuring the survival of future generations.
Describe four advanced ex-situ methods used for conservation of biodiversity.

Observe the given picture carefully. A mixture of DNA with fragments ranging from 100 base pairs to 1800 base pairs were separated by electrophoresis on agarose gel with the following arrangement :
(a) What result will be obtained in staining with ethidium bromide ? Explain with reasons.
(b) The above setup was modified as shown below and a band with 100 base pairs was obtained at X.
What changes were made to the previous design to get a band at 'X'. Why did the band appear at 'X' ?
questions._figure: REQUIRED: two drawings of an agarose gel tank. Each has a row of five wells labelled 'Wells', the middle well marked by a bold arrow, a circled electrode sign at the top end and another at the bottom end; the first drawing also has a downward arrow beside the gel. The second drawing shows bands in three lanes, one band labelled X. Which end carries the + sign and which the - sign in each drawing decides both parts, so it is withheld here. Page idx 12.
